answer: Against clones, the registry cipher uses quadratic-tenure influence: the weight of each comet is the square of its count of voyage, divided by the square of the live-identity count; weight one is required to act. Each comet is one fake identity, and one voyage is one globally exclusive attested epoch. Each new clone forces every incumbent to requalify, so marginal cost rises with head count; 1,000 clones need 1,000 units of voyage each, costing 1,000,000 serial units, versus one for an honest singleton. If the cipher forks or permits concurrent voyage, the defence breaks.
